sections.title: Level 2 Data Sufficiency Strategy
sections.content: At this level, questions are usually solved in 3–4 logical steps. Your goal is only to determine whether the answer can be uniquely determined or not. Pay special attention to hidden variables. Sometimes the information looks complete, but an important value is missing.

sections.title: Time, Speed and Distance (Relative Speed, Boats & Streams)
sections.content: Formula: Distance = Speed × Time. In relative speed, speeds are added when objects move in opposite directions and subtracted when they move in the same direction. In boats and streams: Downstream = (Boat Speed + Stream Speed), Upstream = (Boat Speed − Stream Speed). If only total time is given but distance is not provided, the information may be insufficient. In train problems, even if speed is given, without length the answer may not be determined.

sections.title: Geometry and Mensuration
sections.content: Circle: Circumference = 2πr, Area = πr². If the circumference is given, the radius can be found and then the area can be calculated. In a triangle, the sum of angles is 180°. If two angles are known, the third angle is निश्चित. However, if only the ratio of sides is given without actual values, the area cannot be uniquely determined.

sections.title: Mixtures and Alligations
sections.content: In mixtures, total quantity and ratio are important. If only percentage is given but total quantity is not provided, the final quantity cannot be uniquely determined. In alligation, the ratio is found using the difference method. In Data Sufficiency, check whether both statements together give one definite ratio.

sections.title: Compound Interest vs Simple Interest
sections.content: Simple Interest: SI = (P × R × T) / 100. In Compound Interest, interest is added on previously accumulated interest. If time is 2 years and the rate is given, the difference between SI and CI can be calculated. However, if the principal is not given, the exact amount cannot be determined.

sections.title: Linear Equations with Two Variables (Infinite Solution Trap)
sections.content: If two equations are multiples of each other, they are dependent and produce infinite solutions. Example: 2x + 4y = 10 and x + 2y = 5. Both represent the same equation, meaning they represent the same line. In such cases, the answer cannot be uniquely determined.

sections.title: Hidden Variable Trap
sections.content: 1. Train speed is given but length is missing. 2. x² = 25 is given but x can be ±5. 3. Ratio is given but actual values are missing. Always check whether the answer is unique or if multiple possibilities exist.

sections.title: 3–4 Step Evaluation Strategy
sections.content: Step 1: Understand the question and identify the target. Step 2: Evaluate Statement I alone. Step 3: Evaluate Statement II alone. Step 4: Evaluate both statements together. Only if one unique answer is obtained should the data be considered sufficient.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content: 1. Combining both statements immediately. 2. Assuming actual values from ratios. 3. Forgetting the ± sign in square roots. 4. Treating dependent equations as independent.

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: In Level 2, logic is more important than heavy calculations. Evaluate each statement separately. Watch for hidden variables and infinite solution situations. If only one definite answer is possible, then the information is sufficient.

tricks.title: Relative Speed Check Trick
tricks.explanation: If distance is not given and only time and speed are provided, check whether distance can be determined.
tricks.example: Two trains moving at 60 km/h and 40 km/h — but distance is not given, so the time cannot be determined.

tricks.title: Boat & Stream Identification
tricks.explanation: If both upstream and downstream times are given, boat speed and stream speed can be calculated.
tricks.example: Only downstream time is given — not sufficient.

tricks.title: Think Radius First in Circles
tricks.explanation: If circumference is known, radius can be found first, then the area.
tricks.example: Only area ratio is given — actual value cannot be determined.

tricks.title: Triangle Angle Rule
tricks.explanation: If two angles are known, the third is निश्चित.

tricks.title: Check Total Quantity in Mixtures
tricks.explanation: Percentage alone cannot determine quantity unless the total amount is known.
tricks.example: A 30% solution is given, but total liters are not provided — insufficient.

tricks.title: CI and SI Difference Trick
tricks.example: If P (principal) is not given, the difference cannot be uniquely determined.

tricks.title: Identify Dependent Equations
tricks.explanation: If one equation is a multiple of another, there will be infinite solutions.

tricks.title: Be Careful with ± Sign
tricks.explanation: If x² = 16, then x = 4 or −4. The value is not unique.

tricks.title: Train Length Trap
tricks.explanation: Time from speed can only be determined if train length is also known.
tricks.example: Speed is 80 km/h but train length is not given — incomplete information.

tricks.title: Single Answer Rule
tricks.explanation: If two possible answers exist, the information is insufficient.
tricks.example: x = 5 or 10 are both possible — insufficient.
